description:
## Question

How do Numba (nopython mode), Nx defn, Cython, Pythran, Mojo, Julia (type-stable code) and similar systems define what is allowed in their compiled subset, explain it to developers, and report unsupported constructs? Also: which of them can run the same code in the host language (e.g. Numba's NUMBA_DISABLE_JIT, Nx.Defn.Evaluator), and what that costs or gains. Output: patterns for error messages, subset references, and dual execution, with examples.
title: How do comparable native subsets keep their rules predictable?
